Yucatan Beach and City Properties Privacy Notice
------------------------------------------------

* * *

This Privacy Policy governs the manner in which {domain} collects, uses, maintains and discloses information collected from users (each, a “User”) of the {domain} / website (“Site”). This privacy policy applies to the Site and all products and services offered by the {name}.

### Personal identification information

We may collect personal identification information from Users in a variety of ways, including, but not limited to, when Users visit our site, register on the site, subscribe to the newsletter, respond to a survey, fill out a form, and in connection with other activities, services, features or resources we make available on our Site. Users may be asked for, as appropriate, name, email address, mailing address, phone number. Users may, however, visit our Site anonymously. We will collect personal identification information from Users only if they voluntarily submit such information to us. Users can always refuse to supply personally identification information, except that it may prevent them from engaging in certain Site related activities.

### Non-personal identification information

We may collect non-personal identification information about Users whenever they interact with our Site. Non-personal identification information may include the browser name, the type of computer and technical information about Users means of connection to our Site, such as the operating system and the Internet service providers’ utilized and other similar information.

### Security of your personal information

{name} secures your personal information from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure. Real Estate Experts uses the following methods for this purpose:

*   SSL Protocol

When personal information (such as a credit card number) is transmitted to other websites, it is protected through the use of encryption, such as the Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) protocol.

We strive to take appropriate security measures to protect against unauthorized access to or alteration of your personal information. Unfortunately, no data transmission over the Internet or any wireless network can be guaranteed to be 100% secure. As a result, while we strive to protect your personal information, you acknowledge that: (a) there are security and privacy limitations inherent to the Internet which are beyond our control; and (b) security, integrity, and privacy of any and all information and data exchanged between you and us through this Site cannot be guaranteed.

### Web browser cookies

Our Site may use “cookies” to enhance User experience. User’s web browser places cookies on their hard drive for record-keeping purposes and sometimes to track information about them. Users may choose to set their web browser to refuse cookies or to alert you when cookies are being sent. If they do so, note that some parts of the Site may not function properly.

### How we use collected information

{domain} may collect and use Users personal information for the following purposes:

*   To facilitate account creation and logon process. If you choose to link your account with us to a third party account (such as your Google or Facebook account), we use the information you allowed us to collect from those third parties to facilitate account creation and logon process for the performance of the contract.
*   To send you marketing and promotional communications. We and/or our third-party marketing partners may use the personal information you send to us for our marketing purposes if this is in accordance with your marketing preferences. You can opt-out of our marketing emails at any time.
*   To respond to user inquiries/offer support to users.  We may use your information to respond to your inquiries and solve any potential issues you might have with the use of our Services.

Additionally:

*   To improve customer service
*   Information you provide helps us respond to your customer service requests and support needs more efficiently.
*   To personalize user experience
*   We may use information in the aggregate to understand how our Users as a group use the services and resources provided on our Site.
*   To improve our Site
*   We may use feedback you provide to improve our products and services.
*   To run a promotion, contest, survey or other Site feature
*   To send Users information they agreed to receive about topics we think will be of interest to them.
*   To send periodic emails

We may use the email address to respond to their inquiries, questions, and/or other requests. If User decides to opt-in to our mailing list, they will receive emails that may include company news, updates, related product or service information, etc. If at any time the User would like to unsubscribe from receiving future emails, we include detailed unsubscribe instructions at the bottom of each email or User may contact us via our Site.

### How we protect your information

We only share information with your consent, to comply with laws, to provide you with services, to protect your rights, or to fulfill business obligations.

We adopt appropriate data collection, storage, and processing practices and security measures to protect against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure or destruction of your personal information, username, password, transaction information and data stored on our Site.

### Deletion Request Rights

You have the right to request the deletion of your personal information that we have collected and retained, subject to certain exceptions. Upon receiving and verifying your request, we will delete your personal information from our records, as well as direct our service providers to do the same, unless an exception applies.

We may deny your request to delete your personal information if retaining it is necessary for one or more of the following reasons: (1) Transaction completion: To complete the transaction for which we collected the personal information, provide a requested good or service, fulfill the terms of a warranty or product recall, or perform our contract with you. (2) Security and Fraud: To detect security incidents, protect against malicious, deceptive, fraudulent, or illegal activities, or prosecute those responsible for such activities. (3) Product Improvement: To debug products, identify and repair errors that impair existing intended functionality. (4) Free Speech and Legal Rights: To exercise free speech, ensure the right of another consumer to exercise their free speech rights, or exercise another right provided for by law. (5) California Electronic Communications Privacy Act: To comply with the California Electronic Communications Privacy Act (Cal. Penal Code § 1546 et. seq.). (6) Scientific or Statistical Research: To engage in public or peer-reviewed scientific, historical, or statistical research in the public interest that adheres to all applicable ethics and privacy laws, when deleting the information may render the research impossible or seriously impair its achievement, provided you previously provided informed consent. (7) Internal Use Expectations: To enable solely internal uses that are reasonably aligned with consumer expectations based on your relationship with us. (8) Legal Obligations: To comply with a legal obligation imposed on us. (9) Internal and Lawful Uses: To make other internal and lawful uses of the information that are compatible with the context in which you provided it.

Please note that these exceptions are designed to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect legitimate interests. We will carefully evaluate each request and provide a response in accordance with the relevant regulations.

### Sharing your personal information

We do not sell, trade, or rent Users personal identification information to others. We may share generic aggregated demographic information not linked to any personal identification information regarding visitors and users with our business partners, trusted affiliates and advertisers for the purposes outlined above. We may use third-party service providers to help us operate our business and the Site or administer activities on our behalfs, such as sending out newsletters or surveys. We may share your information with these third parties for those limited purposes provided that you have given us your permission.

We may need to process your data or share your personal information in the following situations:

Third-Party Service Providers. We may share your data with third-party vendors, service providers, contractors or agents who perform services for us or on our behalf and require access to such information to do that work. Examples include payment processing, data analysis, email delivery, hosting services, customer service, and marketing efforts. We may allow selected third parties to use tracking technology on the Services, which will enable them to collect data about how you interact with the Services over time. This information may be used to, among other things, analyze and track data, determine the popularity of certain content and better understand online activity. Unless described in this Policy, we do not share, sell, rent or trade any of your information with third parties for their promotional purposes.

### Third-party websites

Users may find advertising or other content on our Site that link to the sites and services of our partners, suppliers, advertisers, sponsors, licensors and other third parties. We do not control the content or links that appear on these sites and are not responsible for the practices employed by websites linked to or from our Site. In addition, these sites or services, including their content and links, may be constantly changing. These sites and services may have their own privacy policies and customer service policies. Browsing and interaction on any other website, including websites which have a link to our Site, is subject to that website’s own terms and policies.

### How do we handle social logins

If you choose to register or log in to our services using a social media account, we may have access to certain information about you.

Our Services offer you the ability to register and log in using your third party social media account details (like your Facebook or Google logins). Where you choose to do this, we will receive certain profile information about you from your social media provider. The profile Information we receive may vary depending on the social media provider concerned, but will often include your name, e-mail address, friends list, profile picture as well as other information you choose to make public.

We will use the information we receive only for the purposes that are described in this privacy policy or that are otherwise made clear to you on the Services. Please note that we do not control, and are not responsible for, other uses of your personal information by your third party social media provider. We recommend that you review their privacy policy to understand how they collect, use and share your personal information, and how you can set your privacy preferences on their sites and apps.

### How long do we keep your information?

We keep your information for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this privacy policy unless otherwise required by law.

We will only keep your personal information for as long as it is necessary for the purposes set out in this privacy policy unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law (such as tax, accounting or other legal requirements).

When we have no ongoing legitimate business need to process your personal information, we will either delete or anonymize it, or, if this is not possible (for example, because your personal information has been stored in backup archives), then we will securely store your personal information and isolate it from any further processing until deletion is possible.

### Information safety

We aim to protect your personal information through a system of organizational and technical security measures.

We have implemented appropriate technical and organizational security measures designed to protect the security of any personal information we process. However, please also remember that we cannot guarantee that the internet itself is 100% secure. Although we will do our best to protect your personal information, the transmission of personal information to and from our Services is at your own risk. You should only access the services within a secure environment.

### California residents specific rights

If you are a resident of California, you are granted specific rights regarding access to your personal information.

California Civil Code Section 1798.83, also known as the “Shine The Light” law, permits our users who are California residents to request and obtain from us, once a year and free of charge, information about categories of personal information (if any) we disclosed to third parties for direct marketing purposes and the names and addresses of all third parties with which we shared personal information in the immediately preceding calendar year. If you are a California resident and would like to make such a request, please submit your request in writing to us using the contact information provided below.

If you are under 18 years of age, reside in California, and have a registered account with the Services, you have the right to request the removal of unwanted data that you publicly post on the Services. To request the removal of such data, please contact us using the contact information provided below, and include the email address associated with your account and a statement that you reside in California. We will make sure the data is not publicly displayed on the Services, but please be aware that the data may not be completely or comprehensively removed from our systems.

### Advertising

Ads appearing on our site may be delivered to Users by advertising partners, who may set cookies. These cookies allow the ad server to recognize your computer each time they send you an online advertisement to compile non-personal identification information about you or others who use your computer. This information allows ad networks to, among other things, deliver targeted advertisements that they believe will be of most interest to you. This privacy policy does not cover the use of cookies by any advertisers.

### Google adsense

Some of the ads may be served by Google. Google’s use of the DART cookie enables it to serve ads to Users based on their visit to our Site and other sites on the Internet. DART uses “non personally identifiable information” and does NOT track personal information about you, such as your name, email address, physical address, etc. You may opt out of the use of the DART cookie by visiting the Google ad and content network privacy policy at [http://www.google.com/privacy\_ads.html](https://www.google.com/privacy_ads.html "http://www.google.com/privacy_ads.html")

{domain} has the discretion to update this privacy policy at any time. When we do, we will revise the updated date at the bottom of this page. You acknowledge and agree that it is your responsibility to review this privacy policy periodically and become aware of modifications.

### Children under thirteen

{name} does not knowingly collect personally identifiable information from children under the age of thirteen. If you are under the age of thirteen, you must ask your parent or guardian for permission to use this website.

About this property
-------------------

Quinta Portico is beautifully designed in timeless hacienda-style architecture, blending classic Old World charm with modern comfort and efficiency. Designed with versatility in mind, the property features two fully independent living spaces—ideal for extended family, guests, or income potential—while maintaining the comfort and feel of a grand private home.

Each wing of the home is fully independent, offering its own thoughtfully laid out space with a spacious kitchen, two well-appointed bedrooms, two full bathrooms, a bright and inviting open-concept room with a kitchen, and a spacious pantry. The home has large windows and glass doors providing a generous amount of natural light to create a warm, welcoming atmosphere throughout both homes. Each side of the home has its own private covered terrace; one of them features an outdoor kitchen.

  

At the heart of the property lies an impressive 17-meter swimming pool set next to the grand covered terrace. Twin sun terraces flank the pool, offering open-air lounging areas with sweeping views of the neighboring meadow of the polo club, where horses graze peacefully—an idyllic pastoral scene that enhances the hacienda ambiance.  
  
Each side of the home provides a covered terrace; one of them features an outdoor kitchen.

  

The home is equipped with a state-of-the-art solar energy system, including panels, batteries, an inverter, and surge protection, ensuring reliable power and off-grid living. Comfort is further enhanced by a water softener system, pressurized water supply, full air-conditioning throughout, and an automated irrigation system to maintain the landscaped grounds.

  

Additional amenities include a large cistern, ample terrace space, dedicated storage areas, and covered parking for convenience and protection.

  

Quinta Portico is sold fully furnished and move-in ready; this remarkable property presents a rare opportunity to enjoy refined countryside living with modern efficiency and comfort.

Nestled in the serene community of Chuburna Puerto, Casa Talavera is a single-level home that offers the perfect blend of convenience and coastal charm. Situated just 200 meters from the emerald coast of the Gulf of Mexico and a short drive away from the vibrant main plazas of Chuburna and Chelem. 

  

Featuring 3 generous bedrooms, 2 full bathrooms, and 2 additional half bathrooms, this home offers ample space for family and guests. The flexible room/office is ideal for working from home or pursuing hobbies, and can easily be converted into an extra bedroom to accommodate visitors. 

The equipped kitchen, with Mexican flare, flows into the inviting living room and dining areas. Step outside to your private paradise, where a stunning filtered pool awaits. Perfect for entertaining or unwinding after a long day, the lush front and backyards provide a tranquil setting complete with a covered terrace and a BBQ area- perfect for hosting family gatherings. 

  

This home includes 8 solar panels, a water softener, a pressurized water system, pool filtration, furniture, and the convenience of two garage and additional storage. 

  

Location: 

5 minute drive to main plaza of Chelem and Chuburna Puerto

20 minute drive to Progreso 

55 minute drive to Mérida Centro 

60 minute drive to Merida International Airport

DISCOVER Plaza Grande

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

**Zócalo** is a generic term for the buildings surrounding a central plaza. While Mexicans typically use it to refer to **THE Zócalo** in **Mexico City**, visitors unfamiliar with Mérida sometimes use it to indicate the **Plaza Grande**.

**Plaza Grande** is the heart of Mérida, marking the very center of the **Historic District**. It is surrounded by four prominent buildings:

*   **Catedral San Ildefonso**
*   **The Governor’s Palace**
*   **Casa Montejo** (now housing **Banamex**)
*   **MACAY Museum**

Additionally, the **Olimpo**, a cultural center featuring gallery space, a movie theater, and a planetarium, as well as the **Ayuntamiento** (City Hall), also border the plaza.

Plaza Grande is a vibrant gathering place where people come to **meet, relax, get their shoes shined, protest, shop, read the newspaper, sing, dance, chase pigeons, or simply watch the world go by**. The plaza is also home to **newsstands, coffee shops, and small vendors**, offering plenty of opportunities to browse and explore.

DISCOVER Santa Ana

Vibrant Santa Ana
-----------------

Santa Ana church is easily identified by the pyramidal spires as well as the raised platform foundation, most likely a former Maya temple platform. The belief is that Santa Ana was the city’s farm where plantations grew food for the city. In the 1700s, it served the northernmost barrio of colonial Mérida with a large population of indigenous Maya and mulattos.

Several galleries and museums are located in this established and growing art district. Santa Ana also has a lovely small market with vendor stalls, fresh fruits, and vegetables. A popular group of _cocina economics_ (small local kitchens) all serve traditional Yucatecan foods and fresh juices. Just one block to the south, you will find more restaurants and tourist shops along Calle 47, which connects to the Paseo de Montejo.

Vendors set up here frequently – seems to be more of a “pop-up” style market sometimes with no rhyme or reason to the days/times. These vendors are set up in the evenings and weekends as well as other days of the week.

Santa Ana Park is a gorgeous place to visit during Christmas. Fairy lights form a canopy in the plaza over the park’s central area. It is quite magical to visit during the holidays.

DISCOVER San Sebastian

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

In colonial times, **San Sebastián** was part of an area granted by **Francisco de Montejo** to his son. Seeking to establish large estates, he forcibly **removed the Indigenous Maya**, relocating them to what is now known as **San Sebastián**.

For hundreds of years, this area was home to the **disenfranchised local Maya and lower-class immigrants**. Historical accounts describe them as **“passing their days outside the city walls, living in homes of stone and straw, or in the dark and dusty streets and plazas.”**

In the **early 20th century**, **San Sebastián** was considered a dangerous area, earning the nickname **Barrio Bravo**, as young men frequently fought among themselves and against rival barrios. **Rumor has it** that the **metal fence** surrounding the government offices on **Calle 75** was built using repurposed **rifle muzzles from the Mexican Revolution**.

Today, **San Sebastián’s small food market**—offering **fresh fruits, vegetables, butcher shops, and cocina económicas**—is especially **busy on weekend nights**.

##### **Annual Festival: Invocation of Our Lady of the Assumption**

📅 **August 3–15**  
  
Enjoy **San Sebastián’s famous feria**, featuring **voladores** (homemade bottle rockets), **papier-mâché bulls**, and **live music**.

##### **A Neighborhood of Fairs**

San Sebastián is known for its **frequent fairs**. Throughout much of the year, the **park is filled with booths, penny arcades, Ferris wheels, and merry-go-rounds**, creating a lively and festive atmosphere.

DISCOVER La Ermita

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

The names **La Ermita** or **Ermita** are interchangeable. Dedicated to _Nuestra Señora del Buen Viaje_ or _Our Lady of the Good Journey_, the Ermita Church was originally built in the 1700s as a wayfarer’s shrine.

This was the last place to say your prayers before you set out to Campeche, a dangerous trip west at that particular time. Our Lady of the Good Journey is Mérida’s equivalent of Saint Christopher, the patron saint of travelers.

There’s a small, interesting, beautiful garden and patio with access through a wooden door just across from the park. The garden contains medicinal and ornamental plants and trees along with a variety of flowers, ferns, and shrubs; all native Yucatecan species. Entry is free but access is limited. If the door is open, peek your head in and ask to see the garden. Some say the garden has ghosts . . .

The park opposite La Ermita’s church was also renovated a few years ago with a new playground, Wi-Fi connections, and computer docking stations.

The streets around Ermita have been reset and repaved with original bricks. Most people will tell you the bricks were imported from Europe, however the rumor is they purchased from a company in Cincinnati, Ohio!

DISCOVER Santiago

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

Another of the oldest Colonias in Mérida, the church of Santiago, was founded in 1637. Little remains of the original structure other than a modest sanctuary with a baroque statue of Santiago and a dated inscription at the entry.

Approximately 350–400 years ago, Santiago was the area relegated to the indigenous Indios and artisans. Later it was the German district. Before Paseo de Montejo was built around the turn of the century, Santiago was considered the nicest place to live in Mérida.

Calle 59 was the main formal entrance into Mérida after Porfirio Diaz built the Centenario Zoo and Parque de La Paz. The Santiago Market is one of the best in Mérida with a variety of fresh fruits, vegetables, eggs, flowers, fresh juices (made on the spot), and a meat market. A host of excellent _cocina economics_, clothing, sundries, and a _tortilleria_ are found here.

The center of the park has a beautiful water fountain with many trees where you will find people relaxing in the shade.

**Remembranzas Musicales** is every Tuesday at 8:30 PM. This event brings residents and tourists together to dance the cha-cha, the mambo, salsa, and other Latin dances to live Big Band music under the stars.

DISCOVER Santa Lucia

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

It’s no surprise that **Santa Lucia**, the closest **Colonia** to **Plaza Grande**, plays an important role in the history of Mérida's neighborhoods. Both locals and visitors gather here to watch beautiful dancers, learn about Yucatecan history, and enjoy the pleasant weather.

Santa Lucia holds great cultural significance in the city. The **salmon-colored Santa Lucia Church** stands at the corner of **Calle 60 and Calle 55**, just three blocks north of **Plaza Grande**. Across from the church, a small park serves as a venue for music and dancing events, held under the sculpted heads of famous Yucatecan musicians. Artisans’ booths are also set up on **Sundays** and other special occasions.

In recent years, **Santa Lucia Park** has grown in popularity. It is anchored by **La Tratto Santa Lucia**, a restaurant owned by the same family behind **Trotter’s** and **Pancho’s**. The park also features the well-known **Ki'Xocolatl chocolate shop** and many other attractions.

One of the park's most cherished traditions is the **Yucatecan Serenade**, held **every Thursday at 9:00 PM** since **1965**. This open-air event showcases **live music, local history, and traditional costumes**, along with performances of **Yucatecan dances**.

DISCOVER San Juan

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

Located just **four blocks south of Plaza Grande**, the **Church of San Juan** is one of the most breathtaking in **Mérida**. Dating back to **1770**, this **magnificent yellow church** stands out with its architectural details and commanding presence in the park.

The **San Juan Arch** marks the most significant **historic gate to the city**. It was **rebuilt in 1790** during the governorship of **Lucas de Gálvez y Montes de Oca**, the same **Lucas de Gálvez** who initiated the construction of **Mérida’s largest market, Mercado Lucas de Gálvez**.

The **inscription on the arch’s plaque** reads:

> **"The Year 1790. Owing to the personal intervention, zeal, and prudent policy of the Governor Captain General of this Province, the lord don Lucas de Gálvez was able to inspire the generous stimulus of the Pueblo, lovers of the common benefits of liberty, in whose name were provided the funds for the opening and construction."**

In the **San Juan Park**, a **garden and fountain** are adorned by a **bronze statue** known as **“The Little Black Girl of San Juan.”** During colonial times, lantern bearers were entrusted with keeping the peace, announcing, **"It’s twelve o’clock, and all is serene."**

In **1810**, the **chaplain of the church, Don Vicente María Velásquez y Alvarado**, led the **San Juanistas**, a movement attributed to some of the **earliest calls for Mexican independence**.

##### **Annual Event: Paseo de las Ánimas**

**Last week of October**  
  
The **Paseo de las Ánimas** is an important part of **Día de Muertos** celebrations. Participants gather at the **General Cemetery (Calle 81A x 90, Centro)** and walk in a **procession to San Juan Park**, dressed in **traditional Yucatecan clothing with painted skulls on their faces**. Upon arrival, visitors can enjoy **traditional snacks, sweets, cultural performances, and presentations**.

DISCOVER Mejorada

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

The **very first hospital** in **Mérida** was built in **Mejorada** in **1562**. Between **1688 and 1694**, the **Franciscans** constructed two sets of **churches and convents**—one disappeared, but the other, **La Mejorada**, still stands today.

This historic building has served **many purposes** over the years before becoming home to the **Faculty of Architecture at UADY**. It is also connected to another important **Franciscan colonial structure**, the **Dragon Cavalry**, which once served as the **military garrison headquarters of Mérida**.

#### **Exploring Mejorada Park**

This **tranquil park** features a **large bronze sculpture** commemorating the **Niños Héroes de Chapultepec**, often used by **local youth for dance and parade practice**. While there is no **market in the neighborhood**, the **central Mercado Lucas de Gálvez** is just a **few blocks south**.

On the **west side of the park**, you’ll find:

*   The **famous Los Almendros restaurant**, known for its traditional Yucatecan cuisine.
*   The **Museo del Arte Popular**, a museum dedicated to **Mexican folk arts and crafts**.

Mejorada is mostly centered around **local celebrations and events**. To stay informed, **visit the church** and check the **bulletin board** for upcoming activities.

How to Prepare Your Yucatán Home for a Successful Sale
======================================================

By [Stefanie Jiras](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/author/stefanie-jiras/ "Posts by Stefanie Jiras")
[Real Estate](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/category/real-estate/)
, [Selling](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/category/selling/)
 May 1, 2026

![28](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2026/04/28-1.jpg)

**Selling Your Home in the Yucatán: What Really Matters**
=========================================================

Selling a home in the Yucatán is more than just listing it online — it’s about creating a strong first impression that makes buyers feel immediately connected to the property. Whether your home is a colonial in Mérida or a beach house along the coast, thoughtful preparation can make a major difference in how quickly it sells and the price it achieves.

Working with Yucatan Beach and City Properties ensures that every step is handled professionally and strategically.

🌿 **Curb Appeal Sets the Tone**
--------------------------------

The exterior is the first thing buyers see. Simple improvements can make your home feel cared for and inviting:

*   Refresh exterior paint where needed
    
*   Clean façades, patios, terraces, and walkways
    
*   Trim plants and remove debris
    
*   Make sure the entrance feels open and welcoming
    

These small touches create confidence before buyers even step inside.

🏡 **Create a Clean, Comfortable Interior**
-------------------------------------------

When buyers walk in, they should feel relaxed and able to imagine themselves living there. The best way to achieve this is by:

*   Decluttering
    
*   Removing personal items
    
*   Minimizing excess furniture
    
*   Highlighting architectural features like Chukum finishes, pasta tile floors, high ceilings, arches, or tropical gardens
    

Homes in Mérida and the beach areas often have unique character — let those features shine.

🔧 **Address Minor Issues**
---------------------------

You don’t need major renovations, but small fixes help buyers feel the home has been well maintained:

*   Repair leaks
    
*   Ensure doors and windows open smoothly
    
*   Replace burnt-out bulbs
    
*   Touch up paint where needed
    

These simple steps help avoid distractions during showings.

🌬 **Eliminate Odors**
----------------------

In the Yucatán, humidity, pets, and closed-up rooms can create smells that buyers notice immediately. Smell often influences a buyer’s opinion even more than visuals.

A fresh, clean scent helps create a positive emotional response and signals good care.

📸 **Strong Media Presentation**
--------------------------------

Most buyers first encounter your home online, so the visual presentation must be excellent.

**Your agent at Yucatan Beach and City Properties will arrange the media presentation of your home to ensure it looks its best online and attracts qualified buyers.**

This includes coordinating **photography and video**, ensuring your property is showcased clearly and professionally.

✍️ **Compelling Descriptions That Connect**
-------------------------------------------

A strong property description helps buyers imagine the lifestyle your home offers. Our team writes descriptions that highlight:

*   The feeling of the space
    
*   The lifestyle it supports
    
*   The unique features buyers value in this region
    

Real estate marketing is about connection, not perfect grammar. Some of the world’s most successful brands use conversational or intentionally imperfect phrasing because it feels natural and memorable.

What matters most is that the wording captures attention and helps buyers picture themselves living there.

⭐ **The Bottom Line**
---------------------

A well-prepared home:

*   Shows better
    
*   Attracts more buyers
    
*   Sells faster
    
*   **Helps attract qualified buyers and encourages more serious offers**
    

With the right preparation and the guidance of Yucatan Beach and City Properties, selling your home in the Yucatán becomes a smooth, strategic, and successful experience.

**Key Points for Sellers** 
===========================

*   Refresh exterior paint and clean outdoor areas
    
*   Declutter and stage interiors
    
*   Highlight unique features like Chukum, pasta tile, high ceilings, or gardens
    
*   Make small repairs (leaks, lighting, doors/windows)
    
*   Eliminate odors from humidity, pets, or mold
    
*   Ensure the property description is lifestyle‑focused and emotionally engaging
    
*   Allow for marketing‑friendly language that captures attention
    
*   Proper preparation helps homes sell faster and encourages more serious offers

DISCOVER San Cristóbal

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

In the **1540s**, **Francisco Montejo** and his **conquistadores** designated this area to house the **Indigenous people from Central Mexico** who had aided them in conquering the **Maya**.

The **San Cristóbal Church**, also called **Our Lady of Guadalupe**, was the **last** church built by the **Spaniards in Yucatán**, with its foundation stone laid in **1757**.

During the city’s rapid expansion, reaching **San Cristóbal** was difficult due to a **high hill** and a **steep street** known as **“The Street of the Impossible.”** Despite this, the neighborhood became home to **five distinct cultures**: **Maya, Mexican, Spanish, Mestizo, and Arab**. Over time, **Lebanese immigrants** established their **businesses and homes** in **San Cristóbal**, making it a natural choice for their community.

From this **culturally rich Colonia**, two **staples of Yucatecan cuisine** emerged:

*   **The tortilla**
*   **The kibi**_(a Lebanese-inspired dish that became a local favorite)_

##### **San Cristóbal Church – A Mérida Landmark**

The **church’s architecture** is reminiscent of the **Cathedral in Plaza Grande**, featuring a **recessed shell archway** similar to the **church in Umán**. Take a moment to admire the **magnificent Moorish choir window**, which beautifully frames the **Virgin of Guadalupe**.

This church is a **major landmark**, not only for its **architectural beauty** and **patron saint**, but also as the site of the **Virgin of Guadalupe celebrations** on **December 12** each year.

A **stairway of 129 steps** leads to the **nave’s interior gallery**, where a **neoclassical stone retablo**—reportedly sculpted by an **imported European artist**—can be found. The **Latin inscription** above the entrance reads:

> **“This is the House of God and the Gate of Heaven.”**

##### **Annual Event: Virgin of Guadalupe Celebration**

**December 12  
**Each year, thousands gather here to honor **Our Lady of Guadalupe** with **festivities, processions, and religious ceremonies**.

Top Neighborhoods in Mérida for Families, Investors, and Expats
===============================================================

By [Stefanie Jiras](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/author/stefanie-jiras/ "Posts by Stefanie Jiras")

🌴 Best Places to Live and Invest in Mérida and the Yucatán Coast

  
Mérida blends history, culture, and modern living in a way few cities can. And for many buyers, the Yucatán lifestyle extends beyond the city and out toward the Gulf Coast.

Whether you’re moving with your family, looking for an investment, or relocating as an expat, choosing the right area will shape your experience and long‑term satisfaction.

👨‍👩‍👧 Family-Friendly Neighborhoods

Families often prioritize safety, stability, nearby services, and a calm environment. Montebello and Colonia México offer an established residential feel with mature trees, quiet streets, and easy access to everyday conveniences.

  
For a more modern suburban setting, Cholul and Altabrisa provide newer housing options, wider streets, and quick access to hospitals, major shopping centers, and key roadways — ideal for busy family routines.

  
Families who dream of coastal living often look toward Progreso, Chelem, and Chuburná Puerto, where a relaxed pace, ocean breezes, and growing services create a family‑friendly beach lifestyle within easy reach of Mérida’s schools and healthcare.

💼 High-Performing Areas for Investors 

Investors typically look for strong rental demand, tourism flow, and reliable appreciation.

Mérida’s Centro Histórico remains the top performer, especially neighborhoods like Santa Lucía, Santiago, Santa Ana, La Ermita, San Cristóbal, La Plancha, and Itzimná.

These areas offer restored homes, boutique hotels, cultural attractions, and ongoing revitalization — all of which support excellent short- and mid-term rental potential.

  
Along the coast, Chelem and Chuburná Puerto continue to attract investors seeking affordable beachfront or near-beach properties with strong long-term potential.

Seasonal rentals remain steady as more visitors discover the Yucatán’s quieter Gulf beaches.

🌎 Popular Areas for Expats

  
Expats tend to cluster in three lifestyle zones: Centro, the northern suburbs, and the Gulf Coast — each offering a different way to experience life in the Yucatán.

  
Those who want culture, cafés, and a social atmosphere often choose Santa Lucía, Santa Ana, Santiago, or La Ermita.

These areas offer easy access to restaurants, markets, and cultural events, along with the charm of restored historic homes.

  
Expats seeking a quieter, more modern residential environment often prefer the northern part of Mérida, including Montebello, Colonia México, Temozón, and other planned communities.

These neighborhoods offer newer homes, shopping centers, gyms, and convenient access to services.

  
For those dreaming of life by the sea, the Gulf Coast is a major draw. Progreso, Chelem, Chuburná Puerto, and Telchac Puerto attract expats looking for a relaxed beach lifestyle, sea breezes, and a growing year-round community.

🌟 The Bottom Line

  
Each area in Mérida and along the Yucatán coast has its own personality. Understanding these differences will help you choose a location that fits your lifestyle, your goals, and the way you want to experience life in the Yucatán — and Yucatán Beach and City Properties is here to help you find the place that truly feels like home.

Your Complete Guide to Buying Property in the Yucatán in 2026
=============================================================

By [Stefanie Jiras](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/author/stefanie-jiras/ "Posts by Stefanie Jiras")
[Buying](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/category/buying/)
 February 25, 2026

![Centro Merida street](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2026/02/Centro-Merida-street.jpg)

Buying a home in Yucatán is an exciting adventure, whether you’re searching for a colorful colonial condo in Mérida, a beach retreat along the Gulf of Mexico, or a smart investment property. With 2026 shaping up to be a strong year for buyers, now is the perfect time to start planning—but navigating the market can feel overwhelming without the right guidance.

**Understanding the Buying Process**

Foreign buyers can own property in Mexico. If your dream home is within 50 kilometers (about 31 miles) of the coast, or 30 kilometers (about 19 miles) from a border, you’ll purchase through a bank trust called a fideicomiso.

It may sound unfamiliar at first, but the fideicomiso is actually one of the safest and most transparent ways for foreigners to own property in Mexico—and it is fully protected by the Mexican Constitution.

**Why the Fideicomiso Is a Safe and Effective Way to Own Property in Mexico**

A fideicomiso is a bank trust created specifically to allow non‑Mexican citizens to legally own property in restricted zones. It exists because of Article 27 of the Mexican Constitution, which outlines how foreign ownership must be structured. This means the fideicomiso is not only legal—it is constitutionally protected.

**Here’s why it’s such a strong ownership structure:**

*   **You are the legal beneficiary**

You hold all ownership rights. You can sell, rent, remodel, inherit, or transfer the property exactly as you choose. The bank does not own your home—it simply administers the trust.

*   **Long-term, renewable security**

The trust is issued for 50 years and can be renewed indefinitely. Your heirs can inherit the trust without complications, making it a stable, multi‑generational asset.

*   **Protected by the Mexican Constitution**

The fideicomiso exists because the Constitution requires a trust structure for foreign ownership in coastal and border zones. This gives buyers a federally regulated, constitutionally backed path to ownership.

*   **Banks are legally obligated to protect your rights**

The bank cannot make decisions about your property. Its role is administrative and protective, ensuring your ownership rights remain secure.

*   **Simplified inheritance planning**

You designate beneficiaries directly in the trust, which avoids lengthy probate processes and ensures a smooth transfer to your chosen heir.

*   **An extra layer of oversight**

Because a bank is involved, all documents, titles, and legal compliance are reviewed twice: by the notary and by the bank’s legal department. This reduces risk and increases peace of mind.

In short, the fideicomiso is not a barrier—it's a protection. It gives foreign buyers a clear, secure, and legally recognized way to own property in some of the most desirable areas of Mexico.

**Budgeting for Your Purchase**

Closing costs typically range from 5% to 10% of the property value; this percentage is property-specific and does include notary fees, taxes, and registration.

It’s also wise to plan for additional expenses such as:

*   Furniture
*   Minor renovations
*   Setting up a rental property (if investing)

A clear budget helps you avoid surprises and move confidently.

![Map breakdown Merida](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2026/02/Map-breakdown-Merida-242x300.fit.jpg)

**Choosing the Right Location 📍**

Before you begin house hunting, the most important step is deciding the lifestyle you want in the Yucatán. Your preferred way of living will naturally guide you toward the areas that fit you best. For example, think about whether you picture yourself in a historic, walkable city environment, a modern suburban setting with every convenience, or a relaxed coastal lifestyle by the beach. Once you’re clear on that vision, the right location becomes much easier to identify.

Some examples are: 

*   **Centro Histórico (Mérida)**

For those who love historic buildings, colonial architecture, cultural events, and a walkable lifestyle in certain areas. It’s vibrant, busy, and full of museums, markets, cafés, and daily activity—everything is close.

*   **North Mérida**

The modern side of the city offers luxury shopping, high-end restaurants, private hospitals, international schools, and contemporary residential developments. Ideal for buyers who prefer convenience, modern amenities, and a more suburban, polished lifestyle.

*   **Progreso (main port town)**

A bustling coastal city with services, restaurants, and the famous Malecón. Depending on the neighborhood, you may enjoy walkability and an active beach-town atmosphere.

*   **Chelem Puerto**

The busiest of the surrounding beach villages, known for community activities, social gatherings, and a friendly, lively environment.

*   **Chuburná Puerto**

Directly next to Chelem Puerto—slightly quieter, very charming, and still close to everything.

*   **Chicxulub Puerto**

Located on the opposite side of Progreso. Offers classic village‑by‑the‑sea living, a slower pace, and easy access to the beach.

*   **Telchac Puerto**

A quieter, more laid-back beach town farther east along the coast. Known for its peaceful atmosphere, fishing-village charm, and opportunities to find beachfront or near-beach properties at accessible prices. Ideal for buyers seeking tranquility and a slower coastal lifestyle.

Across the coastal villages, buyers often find more affordable options closer to the beach or even beachfront, along with a relaxed, tropical lifestyle.

The key is simple: **Choose the lifestyle you want first—the right location will follow.**

Buying property in the Yucatán is more than a financial decision—it's a lifestyle choice.

With thoughtful planning, the right support from Yucatan Beach and City Properties, and a clear understanding of the market, your dream home or investment property is absolutely within reach.

DISCOVER La Plancha

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

The dream of having the “La Plancha” park has become a reality thanks to the efforts of Governor Mauricio Vila Dosal (Governor of Yucatan from 2018–2024).

The area of the park covers more than 20 hectares of surface, has a linear walkway that runs through the park, a wagon area, and the area where the Gastronomic Market, the Skatepark, the Museum, the walker circular, artificial lake, auditorium, and amphitheater. More than 3 thousand trees were planted, and more than 129 video surveillance cameras were installed.

This large project has many attractions including a 712-meter linear walkway and a circular walkway, a viewing point, an interactive fountain, an amphitheater with capacity for 10,000 people, an artificial lake, a reflecting pool, bathroom modules, and a 2-kilometer recreational trail, skating rink and boardwalk: Gastronomic Market with island, administrative office, restaurants and stores, and the Railway and Light Museums.

Also boasting a sports garden with a multipurpose field for fast soccer, billet, and volleyball; an outdoor gym; a pet park with an area of ​​1,562 meters, and 4 children’s playgrounds. Highlighting history to make it part of the present and future.

This space includes a loading yard, 5 bus bays, access doors to the bays with validators for electronic payment, large waiting rooms, a second floor for the control center, Ie-Tram monitoring, as well as 32 loading areas for the same number of buses.

In this way, Yucatan continues to promote the transformation of mobility, making it sustainable, modern, efficient, thus raising the quality of life that all deserve.

DISCOVER Chembech

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

**Barrio de Chembech** is located in **East Centro**, offering its own **local market**, as well as **small restaurants and cantinas** to enjoy. Right next door, you’ll find a **small but fantastic carnitas taquería**—a favorite among locals.

The **Historic District** is just a **20-minute walk away**, where you’ll find **more tourist-oriented and upscale dining options**. However, **Chembech** maintains its **authentic local charm**, with **friendly residents** who always greet visitors and enjoy casual **evening conversations** as you pass by.

##### **Mercado de Chembech – A Hidden Gem**

Unlike the busier tourist spots, the **Mercado de Chembech** provides an **authentic local experience**, offering a glimpse into **Mérida’s daily life**.

*   **Traditional Foods** – Savor **authentic Yucatecan dishes**, freshly prepared by locals.
*   **Handmade Goods** – Find **unique, handcrafted items** that you won’t find anywhere else.
*   **Warm Hospitality** – Experience the **genuine friendliness** of this charming neighborhood.

Whether you're in search of **delicious local cuisine**, unique artisanal finds, or simply a place to immerse yourself in **Mérida’s everyday culture**, **Barrio de Chembech** is a delightful destination worth exploring.

La Casa de Los Lotos: A Culinary Thai Experience in Baca- You Won't Regret it!
==============================================================================

By [Alejandro Lopez](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/author/alejandro-lopez/ "Posts by Alejandro Lopez")
[Food](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/category/food/)
, [Restaurants](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/category/restaurants/)
 September 18, 2025

![WhatsApp Image 2025-09-18 at 2.17.34 PM](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2025/09/WhatsApp-Image-2025-09-18-at-21734-PM.jpeg)

![Custom Image](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2025/09/WhatsApp-Image-2025-09-18-at-21734-PM.jpeg)

A fantastic reason to get out of the city is **La Casa de Los Lotos Comida Tailandesa**! Located in Baca, once you have tried their food, you will wish they were in your neighborhood. I have to say, it was an incredible and tasteful experience- _I had the best Thai meal ever!_

![Custom Image](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2025/09/WhatsApp-Image-2025-09-18-at-20123-PM-16.jpeg)

The menu is traditional with several classics, and vegetarian options. **Spring rolls** are a great way to start, with a crunchy golden exterior and a honeyed spicy sauce. My favourite entrée is the **Khao Pad Sapparot**, which is basically fried rice mixed with pineapple, chicken and veggies served up in a pineapple shell.

![Custom Image](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2025/09/WhatsApp-Image-2025-09-18-at-20124-PM-15.jpeg)

If you’re in the area and you’re to try something new, you should definitely check out **La Casa de Los Lotos Comida Tailandesa**. It’s a restaurant with authentic Thai food located in the charming town of Baca, just 40 minutes’ drive from Mérida. This is such a peaceful place and after your meal you must walk through the stunning watery gardens, and crystal wall…_don’t be coy about feeding the Koi!_ Dispensers are in the restaurant.

A Day Trip to Xcambó: An Ancient Maya Port on the Yucatecan Coast
=================================================================

By [Alejandro Lopez](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/author/alejandro-lopez/ "Posts by Alejandro Lopez")
[Archaeology](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/category/archaeology/)
, [Explore Yucatan](https://yucatanbeachandcityproperties.com/category/explore-yucatan/)
 February 18, 2026

![Xcambo.33](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2026/02/Xcambo33.jpg)

Nestled in the coastal marshlands of northern Yucatán, Mexico, **Xcambó** flourished as a _center for salt production_ and a _port_ during its occupation. The recovery of a large quantity and variety of foreign objects and materials attests to this place's important economic and political role, as well as its connections with other parts of the Maya realm and Veracruz.

![Custom Image](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2026/02/Xcambo75.jpg)

The first settlement dates to the Middle Preclassic period and experienced growth during the Early and Late Classic period (250–550 CE and 550–700 CE, respectively). Since at least the Early Classic period, the site was not isolated, as it was connected by sacbes, or roads, to three other places: the village of Xtampú, which was administered by **Xcambó**, and the sites of Misnay and Cemul (Dzemul).

![Custom Image](https://assets.agentfire3.com/uploads/sites/2094/2026/02/Xtampu21.jpg)

**Xcambó** is located just 2km north of Dzemul, near the progreso- Telchac highway.

Senior Real Estate Agent, State Certified

Nicholas Sanders
----------------

Nicholas Sanders is a senior real estate adviser with his EC0110.02 certification registered with the state of Yucatán. Nicholas has proudly worked full-time at Yucatan Beach and City Properties since 2017. 

In this time, he has built a reputation for honesty and integrity and as one of the hardest-working agents in Merida!

His goal is to guide buyers on the amazing journey of finding their dream home in the Yucatan, from the initial consultation to the closing and beyond. 

Additionally, Nicholas is an expert in preparing local and foreign sellers to present their homes on the local and international markets.

He guides all of his sellers with documentation needed for the sale, tax strategies, and top-notch listings with professional-quality media. 

Nicholas moved to Merida in 2010 from Indianapolis, Indiana. He takes the love of his adopted home and applies it to his profession by sharing his knowledge of the area with his clients. 

Nicholas now works as a team with his husband, Alejandro Lopez. They live near Centro with their three dogs. Together they have visited over 40 archaeological zones, continue to search for all the best places to eat in Merida, and enjoy living in their home that they fully renovated in 2023. 

Nicholas continues to contribute to the local community with professionalism and trendsetting.

Alejandro Lopez
---------------

Mucho gusto! I am a native to Mérida, Yucatan and I attended the Autonomous University of Yucatan where I completed my PhD in Anthropological Science. After I graduated, I made the move into the real estate industry where I now have teamed up with my husband since 2021. 

As a real estate agent in the Yucatan Beach and City Properties team, my focus is to prepare local and foreign sellers to present their home in the competitive market. I guide sellers regarding documents needed for the sale, tax strategies, and top-notch listings with professional visual media. 

Endeavoring to serve as a guide and resource also for Mexican and foreign buyers, as a local I have developed a deep understanding of the diversity of neighborhoods and areas in Yucatan, and I am passionate for helping clients to find their dream home.

Allow me to offer my professional and personal services to discover your next adventure chapter behind the historic doors of Mérida.

Broker and Director, State Certified

﻿﻿﻿Elizabeth Rodriguez
----------------------

I am the Broker and Founder of Yucatán Beach and City Properties, bringing over 30 years of sales and marketing leadership to every transaction. 

In 2004, a visit to Mérida changed my life. The city's vibrant colors and warm community drew me in, and I knew this was where I wanted to build both a home and a business. 

I personally oversee every transaction from start to finish, working side by side with my agents to ensure no detail is overlooked and your experience is seamless. 

As Broker, I manage every aspect of your real estate journey—from in-depth market analysis to precise contract negotiations—so you can focus on envisioning your future in Mérida or along the Yucatán coast. 

What I Bring to Your Journey 

🏠Guiding clients through seamless buying and selling experiences 

🛡️Personally oversee every transaction to maintain consistency and care 

🤝Open, proactive communication to ease your mind at every step 

Let’s Make Your Real Estate Vision a Reality.

 Whether you're chasing a colonial gem in Mérida, historic hacienda, or a beachside paradise, I'm here to guide you with transparency, dedication, and open communication. 

Reach out today, and let's begin this exciting chapter together.

Are you ready to find your dream?

Nick Besson
-----------

My upbringing in Maine instilled in me a robust work ethic. I have been engaged in the collision industry since the age of fifteen, yet my true passion has always been in buying and selling real estate. In 2008, my wife and I relocated to Florida, which allowed me to pursue my interest in real estate more vigorously. While we have visited numerous countries, we consistently return to Mexico, drawn by its rich culture, welcoming people, exquisite cuisine, and unparalleled natural beauty. In 2017, we acquired our first home in Mexico, and after exploring the Yucatán peninsula, we realized that this was our rightful place. Having experience in buying and selling homes in Mexico, I recognize that each transaction presents its own distinct characteristics. Whether you are looking to buy or sell, I am well-equipped to assist you throughout the process, ensuring a smooth and efficient experience.

Becca Kitto
-----------

Originally from Indiana, I’m a Purdue University graduate with over two decades of professional experience in the mortgage industry and pharmaceutical sales. 

Six years ago, a visit to Mérida changed the course of my life. 

I fell in love with the city’s culture, safety, and sense of community—and ultimately made it my home. 

Today, as a specialized buyer’s agent with Yucatán Beach and City Properties, I help clients confidently navigate the process of finding the right home or investment in the Yucatán. 

Outside of real estate, I’m actively involved in the community through Yucatán Giving Outreach, enjoy teaching Pilates, and love spending my free time traveling and exploring with family and friends.

Stefanie Jiras
--------------

**Stefanie Jiras** is a **State-Certified Real  
Estate Agent and Compliance Support** with Yucatán Beach and City  
Properties. She works with both buyers and sellers, guiding clients through the  
Mérida real estate market while helping ensure every transaction is handled  
with accuracy, transparency, and care.

In addition to supporting clients as an agent, Stefanie supports transaction compliance for both purchase and sale processes. She helps verify that properties are fully sellable and that the documentation and procedures for buyers and sellers meet the highest standards of consistency and professionalism.

Originally from **Iowa, United States**, Stefanie and her husband relocated to Mérida with their cat, Domo, and quickly embraced the city’s vibrant culture and welcoming community. Having personally experienced the relocation process, she understands many of the questions clients face when considering a move or investment abroad and brings both professional guidance and real-life perspective to every transaction.

DISCOVER

Seaside Village of Chabihau
---------------------------

Chabihau in the Mayan language means “where the anteater” (Chab) “makes a way” (haü)

Chabihau, a picturesque coastal town in Yucatan, Mexico, is a unique travel destination. This quiet fishing port, located about 90 minutes from Mérida, is famous for its tranquil atmosphere and the opportunity to immerse yourself in authentic Yucatecan culture.

Far from the hustle and bustle of the most popular tourist destinations, Chabihau offers a unique experience for those seeking a deeper contact with local life and nature. During the week, you will find unmatched peace, while on weekends they come alive with a lively atmosphere.

Enjoy the gorgeous views from the bridge at the port exit, perfect for capturing memorable photographs. On your way to Chabihau, marvel at spotting flamingos along the road.

Take time to enjoy the beauty of the place, such as the trees, posters and signs painted in their characteristic aquamarine green color. With its beautiful waters, sand and sea breeze, Chabihau is ideal for spending a romantic sunset as a couple or sharing unforgettable moments with friends.

Immerse yourself in the beauty and tranquility that this charming coastal town has to offer.

DISCOVER Celestun

The Village of Celestun
-----------------------

Celestun Special Biosphere Reserve is a 146,000-acre park located at the north-western tip of the Yucatan Peninsula in the village of Celestun. About 90 km / 55 miles from Merida, Celestun is a combination of coastal scrub, estuary, and mangrove, which together provides an excellent habitat for wildlife of many sorts. Celestun means "painted stone" in the Mayan language.

Celestun is probably best known for its Flamingos however it is also host to over 300 other species of birds, including the endemic Yucatan Wren, Mexican Sheartail, and Black-throated Bobwhite. In addition to birds, Celestun houses many species of reptiles, including 2 crocodile species: Morelet's and American, 4 sea turtles: Hawksbill, Green, Loggerhead, and Leatherback, iguanas, land turtles, and Boa Constrictors.

At the ocean you will find extensive gorgeous beaches full of coconut trees, with calm and beautiful seas… the beauty of this place is truly a gift.

DISCOVER Puerto de Chelem

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

Chelem, meaning "Here under the magpie," is one of the most important ports in the municipality, attracting visitors year-round.

Many years ago, Chelem Puerto served as a landing site for cattle, fruits, and other goods transported by canoes from Chiapas and Tabasco. Today, the village is known for its broom-making, fishing, hunting, salt flats, and tourism. Many families from Mérida and beyond have vacation homes in this tropical retreat, surrounded by numerous tourist centers.

Annual Festival – A festival is held each year in honor of , the town's.  
August – A festival is held each year in honor of the Virgin of the Miraculous Medal, the town's patron saint.

Chelem is situated west of the shelter port Yucalpetén, between Fraga Lake and the North Coast.

Bob Lissandrello
----------------

Bob Lissandrello was raised in West Sayville, Long Island, New York, and moved to New Hampshire in 1977. He began his career in law enforcement, serving as a Store Detective and later with the New Hampshire State Police Marine Patrol.

Following his lifelong passion for cooking, Bob attended Culinary School in upstate New York and became Chef at the Albany Marriott, earning numerous awards. He later built a successful career with the Knights of Columbus Insurance, becoming one of the top agents in Florida.

In 2008, Bob and his wife Cristy moved to Mérida, Yucatán, where he transitioned into real estate. Since then, he has been proudly serving clients with Yucatán Beach and City Properties. Bob and Cristy, married since Valentine’s Day 2003, live in Vista Alegre North Mérida with their two dogs, Lolita and Coco

Cristina Gasque
---------------

Cristina Gasque is a native of Merida Yucatan and has been in Real Estate here in Yucatan since 2008. 

Being fluent in both English and Spanish, Cristina excels at clients find their dream home and relocating. As a Meridian she knows all the “in’s and outs” of the area, including the beaches. 

She studied Nutrition and recently finished her studies for Magnetic Therapy and Massage. 

She is married to Robert Lissandrello and they live in North Merida with their two dogs Lolita and Coco. 

Cristina loves her home town of Merida, and feels that she is so fortunate to both live and work here.

DISCOVER Puerto Progreso

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

**Progreso** is the **port of entry to Yucatán**, an unbeatable place for practicing the most varied **water sports**: **surfboard**, **windsurfing**, and **kayaking**.  
Here you can **walk along the boardwalk**, **enjoy the breeze**, and **savor delicious regional food** in the many **restaurants** that line the harbor boardwalk.  
Today, it is the **arrival point** for numerous **tourist cruises** from around the world, from which countless **passengers disembark**, enjoying not only its **charm** and its **exquisite taste of a historic port**, but also the **peace** and **friendliness of the city** and **its people**.

There are large **supermarkets**, a **central marketplace**, a **main town square**, **restaurants**, **hospitals**, **hotels**, **banks**, **exchange houses**, **taxis**, **handicraft shops**, and **Municipal Buildings**.

**Puerto Progreso** is the **favorite beach of the Yucatecans**, since during the **holiday season** all families come to enjoy the **sand**, the **sea**, and the **sun**, especially for **Easter** and the months of **July and August**.

DISCOVER Chicxulub Puerto

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

**Chicxulub Puerto Village** in **Municipality of Progreso**

Located very close to **Progreso** is **Chicxulub Puerto**, a village on the **Gulf Coast**.

This small **fishing port** has **sandy beaches** lapped by **crystal clear** and **calm water**.

Its hotel infrastructure is limited, but it has **small hotels**, **condominiums**, and **villas** that will give you **rest** and **tranquility**.

In the local **Mayan language**, **Chicxulub** means either **"the devil’s flea"** or **"tail of the devil"** and refers to a **massive asteroid** that landed here **millions of years ago**.

The **Chicxulub Crater** is a large **meteorite crater**. This is the **center of the impact crater** that scientists believe was made when the **asteroid** that wiped out the **dinosaurs** smashed into the **Earth’s surface**.

It is partly in the **Yucatán Peninsula** in **Mexico** and partly **underwater**.

DISCOVER Dzilam de Bravo

The "Ecotourism" Fishing Village.
---------------------------------

Dzilam de Bravo, a tiny fishing village with a population of around 2,500 people is located on the north coast of Yucatán.  
This is one of the few remaining untouched areas of Yucatán and an absolute hidden gem, making a combination of natural beauty and adventure.  
Enjoy the tranquility and beauty of the beaches in Dzilam de Bravo.  
Explore an eco-tour in the nearby nature reserve, where you can see birdlife and swim in cenotes.  
Discover Xbuya-ha, a freshwater spring that bubbles up into the ocean.  
Take a kayaking tour along the Bocas de Dzilam, where the ocean and river meet.  
Explore the cenote Elepetén located within the mangroves, where various marine species reside.  
Truly a last remaining secret in Yucatan.

DISCOVER San Benito & San Bruno

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

San Benito is located about a 40-minute drive from the city of Mérida, about a 15-minute drive from Progreso, and is part of the Riviera Yucateca.

In the area, you will find beautiful beaches with crystalline water and soft white sandy beaches. The beach is also a nesting site for sea turtles, and visitors can observe the turtles laying eggs during certain times of the year.

With sparkling water, white sand beaches, and palms for shade, as you can imagine, the vibe is completely relaxed.

Visitors can enjoy a variety of activities at San Benito, including swimming, sunbathing, fishing, kayaking, and beach volleyball.

San Benito is also a popular spot for beach weddings.

Many Canadians, Americans, and Europeans who want to escape their chilly winters are attracted to San Benito as a place to live part-time or full-time where they find a place to relax. It is also a favored area of the upper class of Mérida.

In addition to the beautiful beach, there are several attractions nearby, including the Mayan ruins of Chichen Itza and the Cenote Suytun, a natural swimming hole. Visitors can also enjoy hiking and birdwatching in the nearby mangrove forests.

#### Xtampú Region – Natural Wonders & Ancient History

Also very close to this area is the Xtampú region: Xtampú, Xcambó, and the Pink Lagoon

Xtampú is a scenic coastal area in Yucatán, Mexico, located between San Benito to the west and Telchac Puerto to the east.

Known for its tranquil beach, vibrant pink lagoon, centuries-old salt flats, and the Maya ruins of Xcambó.

Here is a mix of natural beauty and historical significance.

#### 1) Laguna Rosada

Near Xtampú you will find the Laguna Rosada. Depending on the time of day, the lagoon shimmers pink, similar to Las Coloradas. This happens when the sun is overhead and the sky is clear.

#### 2) Las Salineras de Xtampú

At the lagoon there is also the saltwork "Las Salineras de Xtampú", here pink salt is extracted. This is another opportunity to see the pink water during the dry season starting in November.

#### 3) Xcambó Mayan Archaeological Zone

Xcambó originated during the Early Classic period between 350 and 550 A.D. as a trading post. It was the primary and largest commercial port on the north coast during the Classic Period.

Scientists say approximately 6,000 people lived here.

In the 16th century, the Spanish built a church on the foundation of an old Mayan ruin, of which the foundation walls are still visible.

DISCOVER Chuburna Puerto

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

**Chuburná Puerto** is a **picturesque fishing village** on the **Yucatán coast**, just a few miles **west of Progreso**. With its **charm and authenticity**, this small town offers visitors a **peaceful retreat away from the crowds**.

##### **Tranquil Beaches & Scenic Sunsets**

The **calm coastline** is perfect for **relaxing, sunbathing, and enjoying the sea breeze**. Strolling along the beach at **sunset** offers one of the **most breathtaking natural spectacles** in the region.

The **soft white sand** and **turquoise waters** provide a **serene escape**, making Chuburná Puerto an ideal destination for those seeking **tranquility by the sea**.

##### **The Chuburná Dunes**

The **Chuburná Dunes** create a **picturesque backdrop**, offering a **perfect space to unwind** under the sun. Visitors can:

*   **Immerse themselves** in the turquoise waters.
*   **Walk along the shore**, letting the waves gently wash over the sand.
*   **Experience the natural beauty** of **Las Dunas**, a truly unique coastal landscape.

Many **families and couples** choose to **camp** here due to the **low tourist influx** compared to other popular beaches. However, **bonfires are not permitted**.

##### **The Islands of Chuburná**

Recently, several organizations **developed a new tourist attraction** in the **Chuburná mangroves**. They have built:

*   **Palapas, tables, chairs, and hammocks** on islands and islets.
*   **Scenic viewpoints** offering panoramic views.
*   **Swings and artistic sculptures**, including **dolphins, lizards, and flamingos**.

Visitors can enjoy **crystal-clear waters**, **abundant wildlife**, and **fresh ceviche or fruit**, making for a truly **unforgettable coastal experience**.

DISCOVER San Crisanto

Life in San Crisanto
--------------------

If you are looking for a place to relax and enjoy the natural beauty of the Yucatan Peninsula, San Crisanto might be the perfect destination for you. San Crisanto is a small fishing village that offers a semi-virgin beach, a mangrove forest, and a salt mine, among other attractions.

Boasting one of the cleanest beaches in Yucatan, where you can swim, sunbathe, walk, or simply admire the beauty. The beach is also known for its spectacular sunsets, as the sea moves back and forms a large sandbar that extends more than 300 meters along the coast.

One of the must-do activities in San Crisanto is to take a boat tour through the mangroves, which are also called the “Venetian Yucatan” because of their beauty and diversity. Along the way, you can see different species of birds, fish, turtles, and even some small swamp lizards. The tour ends at a freshwater spring called Dzonot-Tzik, where you can swim and relax.

Another attraction of San Crisanto is its salt mine, which is a traditional activity inherited from the Maya ancestors. You can visit the salt ponds, which have a pink hue due to the microorganisms that live there. You can also learn about the process of extraction, cultivation, drying, and collection of salt from the local workers.

The restaurants of San Crisanto, focus on fresh seafood and coconut products. You can try dishes such as ceviche, fried fish, coconut shrimp, and coconut ice cream. There are also several shops, markets, and places to buy drinks in this charming town.

About this property
-------------------

Casa Arcoíris is a serene retreat tucked away in the charming neighborhood of Vicente Solís. This residential and commercial neighborhood was founded in 1912 through the merger of the Hacienda San Jerónimo and Quinta San Salvador. Vicente Solís is known for its proximity to downtown and El Cabrío Park. It is a popular area among locals and is considered a traditional neighborhood in Mérida. 

This home features two bedrooms, and a full bathroom, offering a peaceful and private setting while still being conveniently close to Downtown, dining, and everyday conveniences of Mérida’s vibrant surroundings.

Step inside to discover a bright, airy interior filled with natural light, creating a warm and inviting ambiance throughout. The thoughtfully designed layout maximizes both space and functionality, making it ideal as a full-time residence, vacation getaway, or investment opportunity.

  

Outdoors, your private oasis awaits. Enjoy a refreshing dipping pool—perfect for cooling off during warm Yucatán days or relaxing in the evening under the stars. The property also features the rare and valuable benefit of off-street parking.

  

Located on a quiet street in Vicente Solís, Casa Arcoíris offers the perfect balance of peaceful living with quick access to the best of Mérida.

*   3.0km to La Mejorada Park   
    
*   3.7km to La Plancha Park

DISCOVER Santa Clara

Art, Culture and Community Spirit
---------------------------------

Located about 90 minutes from Merida, Santa Clara's colorful history dates back to the ancient Mayan civilizations that flourished in this region. Serving as sanctuaries, the coastal landscapes held a deep significance for the Maya. Through it past, Playa Santa Clara Yucatán beckoned traders and explorers that crossed through the Gulf of Mexico.

Visitors can enjoy a variety of activities that highlight the region's natural beauty and cultural richness. A very popular area for water activities such as exploring marine life and coral reefs with snorkeling, kitesurfing, paddleboarding, boat tours, and of course many traditional Yucatecan dishes.

As the Yucatán Coastal areas have been undergoing a transformation several projects are set for the Santa Clara port in the municipality of Dzidzantún.

These projects mark an extension of the ongoing real estate developments that began in Progreso and have now reached Santa Clara, attracting new national and international inhabitants.

About this property
-------------------

Casa Yaxlum is a contemporary design home located in a gated community in Conkal, providing peace of mind and a tranquil ambiance to enhance your living experience. This two-story residence features 3 spacious bedrooms and 3.5 bathrooms. 

Abundance of natural and refreshing airflow through the sliding glass doors and windows create a vibrant open concept layout on the ground level. The heart of the home is a stylish kitchen equipped with modern appliances, elegant countertops, and ample storage.

The open layout seamlessly connects the dining area and living room, facing to the outdoor living area. Unwind in the outdoor oasis surrounded by lush landscaping and an inviting, sparkling swimming pool.  

The second level offers retreats for the homeowners and guests. The spacious bedrooms have ample closet space, and each one has a bathroom that showcases contemporary fixtures and finishes, with a tasteful design that merges functionality with elegance. 

  

Casa Yaxlum harmonizes style, comfort, and functionality, making it a must-see!

About this property

Casa Bosques - Charming Renovated Home

Charming Renovated Home with Jacuzzi in Bosques de Yucatán – West Mérida

Located on a peaceful residential street in the desirable neighborhood of Bosques de Yucatán, this beautifully renovated 2-bedroom, 1-bathroom home offers comfort, convenience, and exceptional value in Mérida’s west side.

  

Fully remodeled in 2021, the home features elegant new flooring, warm wood finishes, and a modernized kitchen, creating a welcoming and functional living space ideal for both full-time living or a comfortable retreat in the city.

  

One of the standout features of this property is the large private Jacuzzi, perfect for relaxing and unwinding after a long day. The home also includes a private office with its own independent entrance, making it ideal for working from home, running a small business, or creating a private studio space.

  

The property is conveniently located near shopping centers, restaurants, supermarkets, and essential services, offering the perfect balance between a quiet residential environment and easy access to everything Mérida has to offer.

Additional highlights include covered parking for two vehicles, security bars on all windows, multiple air-conditioning units, and abundant storage space, making this a practical and comfortable home ready to move into.
